settings.text:

Flip through the 28 missions. Use the handy icons to find one that won’t destroy your house (or your sanity). Then rip it out and get to it.

🎯#2 - Follow the script

No brainstorming required. You get the script, the steps, and what you need. Just follow along and make it happen.

🏅 #3 - Claim your victory

Mission complete. Slap the sticker onto your Epic Dad poster and make the win official.

🖼️ #4 - Put it on display

Hang the poster where your kid sees it every day. Every sticker becomes proof of another “Me and Dad did that” memory.

settings.heading: What’s Inside
settings.content:
A tear-out mission book built for real dads and their kids.

Inside, you’ll find funny, practical challenges designed to turn ordinary moments into memorable dad–kid adventures. Complete missions, collect stickers, fill the achievement poster and work your way towards the ultimate title: Best Dad in the World.

No perfect parenting required. Just questionable decisions, real bonding and stories worth remembering.

settings.heading: Shipping & Returns
settings.content:
Orders are normally shipped on the next business day and delivered within approximately 5–7 business days.

We offer a 30-day return period on full-price items. To qualify for a return, the book must remain unused, unopened and in its original plastic wrapping. No pages may be removed, no stickers used, and the poster must be unused and unmarked.

Return shipping costs are covered by the customer. Sale items, discounted products, gift cards and personalized items cannot be returned.

To request a return or report a damaged or incorrect order, contact info@bestdadbook.com before sending anything back. Approved refunds are issued to the original payment method after the returned item has been received and inspected.

settings.title: What age is this book best for?
settings.answer:
This book shines for kids ages 1–10 — the years when the brain forms the strongest emotional memories and when your presence matters most. The golden years where they still think you’re interesting.
Old enough to have fun, young enough to believe you’re a superhero.

settings.title: Does this work for toddlers?
settings.answer: Yes. If they can laugh, point, splash, or destroy something gently — they qualify.

settings.title: Does this work for older kids (8–10+)?
settings.answer: Absolutely. Older kids get even more into the missions, the secrecy, the challenges, and the sticker collecting.

settings.title: Is this book good for stepdads, bonus dads, or weekend dads?
settings.answer:
Absolutely.
A dad is anyone who shows up and creates memories.

This book works for:

  • stepdads,
  • divorced dads,
  • weekend dads,
  • co-parents,
  • adoptive dads,
  • future dads.

settings.title: Does it work for moms too?
settings.answer: Yes — but moms have a dedicated version of the book.

settings.title: Is this book good for brand-new dads or seasoned veterans?
settings.answer: Both! Fresh dads will find survival hacks, seasoned pros will level-up their dad game, and everyone gets bonus points from their significant others. Win-win-win.

settings.title: How does this book actually help kids remember Dad?
settings.answer:
Kids don’t store memories from words. They store sensory, emotional, surprising moments. This book intentionally includes:

  • ripping pages,
  • shocks + surprises,
  • silliness,
  • laughter,
  • tiny victories,
  • and a sticker ritual that locks the memory.

The poster acts as a daily reminder, strengthening the memory every time your kid sees it.

settings.title: What’s the psychological benefit for kids?
settings.answer:
Research shows kids who share frequent positive, sensory-rich experiences with parents develop:

  • higher emotional security,
  • stronger self-esteem,
  • deeper trust,
  • better resilience,
  • and stronger long-term bonding.

This book delivers those experiences without planning, guilt, or mental load.

settings.title: What’s the psychological benefit for dads?
settings.answer:
The book helps dads:

  • feel competent,
  • avoid decision fatigue,
  • show up consistently,
  • experience micro-wins,
  • build connection without pressure.

settings.title: How does this help with bonding?
settings.answer:
Bonding happens through shared emotional experiences.
This book gives you 28 of them.

Every mission ends with a sticker — a visual anchor that says: "Dad did this with me."

settings.title: Will my kid really remember this?
settings.answer:
Yes. Research shows emotional, sensory, high-engagement activities form stronger memories.

And the poster refreshes the memory daily.

settings.title: Is this book actually useful, or just another dad-gag gift?
settings.answer: Glad you asked! Sure, it’s funny as hell, but beneath the sarcasm is a stack of truly useful, step-by-step activities. It’s practical dad-ing, served with a side of laughs.

settings.title: Why is it better than toys?
settings.answer: Toys fade. Experiences last. This book creates memories kids keep for life.

settings.title: Why is this book more than just a gift for Dad?
settings.answer: It’s not just a gift for him — it’s an investment in your child’s happiest memories.

settings.title: Is this a parenting book?
settings.answer: It is more. It is the Dad-Child Memory Engine.

settings.title: What is the Dad-Child Memory Engine?
settings.answer: It is the system at the heart of the book — a simple, science-backed loop that turns any small moment into a core memory your kid will keep for life.

settings.title: How does the Memory Engine work?
settings.answer: Through a six-step cycle designed around how kids actually form memories: Feel → Do → Laugh → Succeed → Sticker → Remember.

settings.title: Why is this Memory Engine so powerful?
settings.answer: Because it activates the exact combination proven to create long-lasting emotional memories: senses + emotions + imagination + accomplishment + repetition.

settings.title: How many times can we reuse the book?
settings.answer:
It’s a tear-out, one-time adventure book — the experience is the product.
The missions are one-and-done — you rip them out, you do them, you keep them. The book becomes a trophy of memories, not a repeatable workbook.

The memories? Those last forever (and so does your Epic Dad poster).

settings.title: What’s included in the book?
settings.answer:
• 28 tear-out missions
  • Giant Dad Achievement Poster
  • Sticker Pack
  • Scripts + instructions + surprises
  • QR system for saving memories

settings.title: Will my kid actually care about the poster?
settings.answer:
Yes. The poster becomes:

  • a progress tracker,
  • a pride wall,
  • a visual memory machine,
  • and a daily dopamine hit.

settings.title: What makes the sticker so important?
settings.answer:
The sticker is a psychological anchor.
It seals the memory through:

  • reward,
  • ritual,
  • ownership,
  • physical action.

Kids remember moments better when they mark them.

settings.title: What’s the deal with ripping out pages? Am I destroying the book?
settings.answer: Exactly. But think of it as productive destruction. You rip it, you own it, and now you're fully committed. It's like burning ships, but less dramatic.

settings.title: Can I reorder the stickers or get extra?
settings.answer: Yep. If you’ve got multiple kids, lost half your stickers under the couch, or your child used them all on the dog — we’ve got you. Extra sticker packs are sold separately.

settings.title: What if I’m overwhelmed or super busy?
settings.answer:
Perfect. Missions are purposely:

  • low prep,
  • low brain power,
  • high bonding.
    You can do one in 5 minutes.

settings.title: Do I need special tools or equipment? Or a trip to Home Depot?
settings.answer: No. Everything is designed around stuff already in your home.Worst case? MacGyver mode. Kids love that.

settings.title: How long do these activities take? My schedule's chaos.
settings.answer: We’ve got you. Each activity clearly indicates whether it's a quick-and-easy five minutes or a full-day adventure. Choose according to your current chaos-level.

settings.title: Is it safe?
settings.answer:
Yes — but use normal parental common sense.
We’re not responsible for anyone microwaving crayons.

settings.title: Are the missions messy?
settings.answer:
Some. No glitter.
We’re not cruel.

settings.title: What if my kid has a short attention span?
settings.answer: Great — missions are quick and flexible. And surprising and funny.

settings.title: What if I feel awkward doing missions?
settings.answer: Your kid doesn’t judge. They just want YOU.

settings.title: Does this book work for dads who aren’t “crafty”?
settings.answer: Absolutely. Zero crafting talent required. If you can read a sentence, rip a page, and locate tape, you’re qualified. This isn’t Pinterest — it’s dad-ing. Built for real men who don’t own a glue gun.

settings.title: Is this a good gift for dads?
settings.answer:
It’s one of the best dad gifts because it keeps on giving:

  • it creates memories,
  • it boosts confidence,
  • it reduces mental load,
  • it makes Dad the hero of the story.

settings.title: Will my partner like this?
settings.answer: Yes — it reduces the mental load and gives Dad a clear, easy way to bond.

settings.title: Why should I buy this today?
settings.answer: Because kids will only be this small once! Core memories happen in small windows — this book opens those moments for you and turns them into memories they’ll keep for life.

settings.title: He doesn't like to read. Why would I buy this book?
settings.answer: Because this is the book for men who don’t like books. No long parenting lectures. No theory. Just 28 easy, funny missions he can choose, tear out, and do with the kids. Minimal reading. Maximum dad glory.

settings.title: Will he actually read it?
settings.answer: Yes. It’s written by comedians, which means it’s scientifically optimized for maximum toilet-based reading enjoyment.

settings.title: Where’s this masterpiece made, and how long till it lands at my doorstep?
settings.answer: Lovingly crafted (by exhausted dads, mostly) in Europe. We ship worldwide—delivery time depends on your location and whether the mailman decides to stop for coffee along the way.
